procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and order dated January 22, 1968, and December 12, 1968, of the Patna High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 116 of 1966.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The Patna High Court acquitted two of the accused. The conviction of the appellant for offences under section 326 read with section 149 and 148 Indian Penal Code was maintained. The sentence of the appellant for the offence under section 326 read with section 149 Indian Penal Code was reduced from five years to three years. The sentence for the offence under section 148 Indian Penal Code was, however, maintained. The conviction of the other three accused was maintained for some of the offences, and they were awarded sentences of imprisonment on that count. An application was made on behalf of the appellant that his case be dealt with under the Probation of Offenders Act on the ground that he was below 21 years of age at the time of his conviction by the trial court. This application was rejected by the High Court on the ground that the offence for which the appellant had been convicted was punishable with imprisonment for life, and as such, the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act could not be invoked in his case.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court after the High Court certified the case to be fit for appeal under Article 134 (1)(c) of the Constitution of India because it involved a question relating to the applicability of the Probation of Offenders Act. The short question before the Supreme Court was whether the appellant, who was less than 21 years of age on the date of his conviction for an offence under section 326 read with section 149 Indian Penal Code, could get the benefit of section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.

issue.issue_text: Whether an offender under 21 years of age, convicted for an offence punishable with imprisonment for life (in this case, under Section 326 read with Section 149 IPC), is entitled to the benefit of Section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Act.

facts: The appellant was under 21 years of age (19 years old) at the time of his conviction.
He was convicted for an offence under Section 326 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
The punishment for an offence under Section 326 IPC can be imprisonment for life.
The appellant sought to be dealt with under the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, but the High Court rejected his application on the grounds that the offence was punishable with life imprisonment.
law: The Court analyzed Section 6(1) of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.

This section states that when a person under 21 is found guilty of an offence 'punishable with imprisonment (but not with imprisonment for life)', the court should not sentence them to jail without special reasons.
The key legal provision is the explicit exclusion of offences punishable with imprisonment for life.
application: The Court determined that the eligibility for the benefit of Section 6 depends on the maximum possible punishment for the offence, not the actual sentence imposed.

Since the appellant was convicted of an offence under Section 326 IPC, which is punishable with imprisonment for life, his case falls squarely within the exception carved out by the phrase '(but not with imprisonment for life)' in Section 6(1).

The Court reasoned that even though the purpose of the Act is to prevent young offenders from becoming hardened criminals, this benefit is not available for those convicted of very serious offences, such as those punishable with life imprisonment.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the appellant could not invoke the benefit of Section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Act because he was convicted of an offence punishable with imprisonment for life. The Court affirmed that the clear language of the statute excludes such offenders from its provisions, regardless of their age.

arguments.issue_text: Whether an offender under 21 years of age, convicted for an offence punishable with imprisonment for life (in this case, under Section 326 read with Section 149 IPC), is entitled to the benefit of Section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Act.
appellant_arguments: The appellant argued that because he was below 21 years of age at the time of his conviction, his case should be dealt with under the Probation of Offenders Act.
respondent_arguments: The respondent's position, as upheld by the High Court, was that the provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act could not be invoked because the offence for which the appellant was convicted was punishable with imprisonment for life.

cases.case_name: Som Nath Puri v. State of Rajasthan
cases.principle: The provisions of the Probation of Offenders Act are not applicable to a person found guilty of an offense punishable with imprisonment for life.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The benefit of the Probation of Offenders Act is not available for an offense if imprisonment for life is a possible punishment; the fact that a lesser term of imprisonment can also be awarded for the same offense does not take it out of this exclusionary category.
obiter: The Probation of Offenders Act was enacted with the object of preventing youthful offenders from becoming hardened criminals as a result of their association with mature criminals in jail.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The appellant cannot invoke the benefit of Section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Act. An offender under 21 is not entitled to the benefit of the Act if convicted of an offense for which imprisonment for life is a possible punishment. The fact that a lesser term of imprisonment can also be awarded for the offense does not take it out of the category of offenses punishable with imprisonment for life, thereby making the Act's benefits unavailable.
legal_tests_applied: The court applied a statutory interpretation test to Section 6 of the Probation of Offenders Act, focusing on the plain meaning of the phrase 'punishable with imprisonment (but not With imprisonment for life)'. The determinative factor is whether life imprisonment is a possible punishment for the offense, not whether it is the sole or mandatory punishment.
